title: Introduction to Functions
description: Relations, notation, domain and range, parent functions, transformations, and inverses. This is the vocabulary every later unit uses.
prerequisites: Grade 10 algebra basics and reading points on a graph.

lessons.title: Functions and relations
lessons.summary: Decide whether a relation is a function and justify it from ordered pairs, tables, mappings, graphs, and equations.
focus: Identify domain and range in discrete relations.
Use the one-input/one-output rule in tables, mappings, and ordered pairs.
Use the vertical-line test and explain why it works.
Distinguish one-to-one, many-to-one, and one-to-many relations.
lessons.pause: Before each example is classified, cover the answer and state the exact input that proves your decision.
lessons.pitfall: Repeated outputs are allowed. A function fails only when one input has more than one output.

lessons.title: Function notation
lessons.summary: Read and evaluate functions from equations, graphs, and sets; solve for inputs; substitute expressions; and evaluate composite functions.
focus: Interpret f(a) as an output and solve f(x)=k for an input.
Substitute numbers and algebraic expressions using brackets.
Read function values and inequalities from a graph.
Evaluate f(g(x)) and explain why composition order matters.
lessons.pause: Write the substituted expression with brackets before simplifying.
lessons.pitfall: f(2x) means the input is 2x. It does not mean 2f(x). In f(g(x)), g happens first.

lessons.title: Domain, range, and interval notation
lessons.summary: State domain and range from sets, graphs, and equations; use interval notation; and explain contextual restrictions.
focus: Read open/closed endpoints and arrows correctly.
Convert among inequalities, set-builder notation, number lines, and intervals.
Find natural domains and ranges of linear, quadratic, square-root, absolute-value, and reciprocal functions.
Classify a graph as a function while stating its domain and range.
lessons.pause: Project the graph onto the x-axis for domain and onto the y-axis for range.
lessons.pitfall: Infinity is never included, so it always uses a parenthesis. Domain is about inputs; range is about outputs.

lessons.title: Parent functions
lessons.summary: Recognize the core parent functions instantly and state their key points, domains, ranges, symmetry, and asymptotes.
focus: Sketch y=x, y=x², y=sqrt(x), y=|x|, and y=1/x from memory.
State domain, range, intercepts, symmetry, and asymptotes.
Match a graph, equation, table, and description of the same parent.
Use the parent as the starting point for transformations.
lessons.pause: Before each graph appears, sketch its shape and label three anchor points.
lessons.pitfall: The reciprocal parent has asymptotes x=0 and y=0; it never touches either axis.

lessons.summary: Understand what a, k, d, and c do in y=a f(k(x-d))+c before attempting full graphing questions.
focus: Identify vertical and horizontal translations.

lessons.pause: Predict the move before the transformed graph appears.
lessons.pitfall: Inside changes act horizontally and use the reciprocal scale. f(4x) compresses horizontally by 1/4.

lessons.title: Graphing transformations
lessons.summary: Use mapping rules and anchor points to graph combined transformations accurately, including new domains, ranges, vertices, and asymptotes.
focus: Use (x,y) -> (x/k+d, ay+c) for y=a f(k(x-d))+c.
Transform anchor points instead of guessing the shape.
Move vertices, endpoints, and asymptotes correctly.
State the transformed domain and range.
lessons.pause: Build a point table and transform every anchor point before viewing the finished graph.
lessons.pitfall: In the point mapping, x is divided by k before adding d. Missing the reciprocal is the most common lost-mark error.

lessons.title: Inverse functions
lessons.summary: Reverse a function numerically, graphically, and algebraically; swap domain and range; and decide whether the inverse is also a function.
focus: Create an inverse by swapping x and y values.
Reflect a graph in y=x and swap domain with range.
Find an algebraic inverse by swapping x and y, then solving for y.
Use the horizontal-line test and restrict a quadratic domain when necessary.
lessons.pause: Find the inverse yourself before the video completes the algebra.
lessons.pitfall: f^-1(x) means inverse function, not 1/f(x). A quadratic needs a restricted domain for its inverse to be a function.

title: Algebraic Expressions
description: Polynomial operations, factoring, rational expressions, and rational-function graphs. These are the algebra tools underneath quadratics and exponentials.
prerequisites: Grade 10 factoring, distributive property, fractions, and exponent rules.

lessons.title: Adding and subtracting polynomials
focus: Combine only like terms.
Add and subtract polynomials by aligning degree and sign.
lessons.pause: Rewrite subtraction as adding the opposite before combining. Check the highest degree and constant term.
lessons.pitfall: x and x² are different terms even though both contain x.

lessons.title: Multiplying polynomials
focus: Distribute every term and collect like terms.
Use FOIL as a special case of the distributive property.
lessons.pause: Multiply term by term on paper before watching the combination step.
lessons.pitfall: Middle terms can cancel; do not drop them before you combine.
